newsitem.title: USA: Ariz. looks to begin electricity revamp in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Ariz. looks to begin electricity revamp in 1999.

text.p: The Arizona Corporation Commission announced Thursday plans to adopt rules phasing-in customer choice on electricity service beginning January 1, 1999.
Commission chairman Renz Jennings said, "This decision keeps Arizona moving forward into electric competition at the same pace that is occurring nationally and in our neighboring states."
Under the Arizona plan, utilities would have to make 20 percent of their peak 1995 demand available to all customers on a competitive basis, with no more than half sold to large customers.
Beginning in 2001, utilities would have to make 50 percent of their peak 1995 demand available in the competitive market. That would increase to 100 percent by January 1, 2003.
The Commission said utilities will be required to file proposals for services by December 31, 1997.

Utilities will be allowed to recover "stranded investment" costs from customers who participate in the competitive market, although these costs could be offset by expanding wholesale or retail markets, the Commission said.
Public hearings on the rules will be held throughout the state during December, after which the Commission will adopt final rules.
